text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE FIRED — reserved_capacity_throttle for tenant=acadia on cluster=dedicated-acadia-1. Severity=high. Symptoms: elevated P95 latency, 503s, queue growth. Pager: PagerDuty incident: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD12345

PagerDuty: Incident PD12345 created by incident-bot at 2024-10-12T17:04:12Z — routing to eng-oncall. Escalation policy: dedicated-cluster-critical.

Maya: ack'd via PagerDuty — I'm on it. Starting triage. (oncall, step 1) :white_check_mark:

Ryan: Seeing the same; metrics show sustained cpu_gpu_utilization ~98% on pool nodes and reserved queue depth creeping. 503s concentrated to tenant acadia only.

Alex (eng-runtime): Past 20m there's a spike of long-running generation jobs from `acadia-prod-v2`. Looks like a synthetic workload hitting with long seq lengths ( > 4096 ) — KV cache growth is causing memory pressure. Logs:
```
2024-10-12T16:50:02Z runtime WARN kvcache: eviction_rate 0.72
2024-10-12T16:52:14Z runtime ERROR request_dispatcher: queue_depth=87 tenant=acadia target_model=prod-v2 status=throttled
```

Liz (eng-infra): Autoscaler didn't open burst nodes. I see `autoscaler: pool=dedicated-acadia-1 desired=10 current=8 backoff=120s` and GCE quotas are fine. There's an error in the scaler controller talking to the provisioning API: `403: quota allocation denied` from our internal allocator for ephemeral_burst. Investigating.

Jen (sre): Impact window estimate: ~16:50 — ongoing. Customer-facing errors = increased 5xx, median latency for acadia up from 300ms to 1.2s, P95 > 3s. Traffic routing still tries primary pool; fallback path exists but disabled in policy for this tenant (contracted reserved-only).

Tom (cs): Contact thread with Acadia is open — they're seeing timeouts, customers reporting timeouts in their app. They requested priority fix. We need ETA for mitigation.

Maya: Immediate mitigations I can do now: 1) enable soft-throttle for Acadia (limits concurrency per-tenant) 2) temporarily allow routing to shared-burst pool 3) swap Acadia requests to prod-v2-quant (lower memory, lower latency) — need approvals for #2 because it's a contract exception. Any objections?

Alex (eng-runtime): #3 (model switch) is the fastest and lowest-risk. We have prod-v2-quant compatible checkpoint live in the model-catalog. To switch for live traffic:
```
redwoodctl route update --tenant=acadia --route=dedicated-acadia-1 --model=prod-v2-quant --drain=true
```
This will keep existing in-flight requests on current model. Expected reduction in mem pressure ~30%.

Liz (eng-infra): I can try to force a burst allocation manually while I debug allocator. This requires a quick ops runbook permission, which Maya has. If we add burst nodes, we should see queue reduce in ~90s. Doing `allocate-burst --pool dedicated-acadia-1 --count 3` now.

Maya: Granting runbook permission. Liz, go ahead. Also I'm enabling soft-throttle for acadia to cap concurrency at 8 for the moment: `tenant_config acadia set concurrency_limit=8`

Ops-rotation-next: noted — I'll take next shift at 18:00 and follow up for recovery verification.

(3m later)
Liz (eng-infra): `allocate-burst` returned partial success — 2/3 nodes provisioned. Provision logs show `node init failed: disk-image-pull timeout` for one instance. Node count now 10 -> 11. GPU util dropped from 98%->89% across pool.

Alex (eng-runtime): Model swap rolling: `route update` started. New requests to prod-v2-quant. Early telemetry: request mem usage down ~28%, KV evictions decreased. Queue depth down from 87 -> 24.

Ryan: Latency improving: median ~480ms, P95 ~1.1s. 5xx rate for Acadia dropping. Monitoring displays green for error rate but still elevated compared to baseline.

Tom (cs): Relayed to Acadia: "We've enabled a temporary degraded model and added capacity; your traffic should stabilize. We'll confirm with you in 15m." They acknowledged.

Maya: Paging note — since we touched burst allocation and routing & made a contract exception, we need an incident RCA follow-up and a comms note for Acadia. I'll own the RCA ticket. Jen, can you own the postmortem?

Jen (sre): I can own the PM. I'll gather metrics: autoscaler logs, allocator errors, KV cache tracers, routing change timeline. Put a placeholder ticket: INC-2123-RCA.

(ack from PagerDuty)
PagerDuty: PD12345 acknowledged by Maya at 2024-10-12T17:07:03Z.

(15m after mitigation)
Alex (eng-runtime): Stabilized. Queue depth steady <10, GPU util ~70%. No further 503 spikes. Rolling back temporary soft-throttle?

Maya: Keep soft-throttle for 10 more minutes, then we'll remove if stable. Liz continue investigating the disk-image timeouts and allocator 403. Need root cause: why burst quota request denied.

Liz (eng-infra): Found allocator bug: under contention, the allocator returns `403` during token refresh if token cache had concurrent evictions. Patch ready: allocator#fix/refresh-token-concurrency. I'll stage to canary infra tomorrow. Filed infra-T123.

Jen (sre): I'll schedule RCA for tomorrow 10:00 with eng-runtime and infra. Invite list: Alex, Liz, Maya, Ryan, Tom.

Tom (cs): Client update sent: "We applied a temporary model and capacity bump; performance restored. We will follow up with a detailed RCA and timeline of changes." Acadia replied :thumbsup:.

Maya: Handing off to Ops-rotation-next for watch. If anything re-escalates, repage. Thanks team. Closing thread once all followups scheduled.

Ops-rotation-next: Watching. I'll mark incident resolved in PagerDuty once RCA ticket exists and postmortem owner assigned.

(closure)
Maya: PD12345 resolved at 2024-10-12T17:45:01Z — mitigation successful, impact window: 16:50—17:20. Follow-ups: infra-T123 (allocator bug), INC-2123-RCA (postmortem), cust-comm note (Tom).
